edgeFunctions.name: enrich-cast-cron
edgeFunctions.purpose: Server-side sweep that backfills "Cast & Creative" for theatre tickets. WHY THIS EXISTS: cast enrichment used to be client-on-demand ONLY — the event-details screen called enrich-cast when a theatre ticket had no cast. So any theatre ticket never opened in-app on a cast-enabled build stayed empty forever (in prod, 20 of 25 theatre tickets had zero cast). This runs server-side on a schedule and enriches every theatre ticket regardless of how it was created (gmail / imap / photo / manual / calendar). It does the SAME enrichment as enrich-cast INLINE (Wikidata grounding + Claude + the is_known guard, via the shared ./core.ts) rather than calling enrich-cast over HTTP: that hop 401'd at the gateway because enrich-cast is verify_jwt=true and a service-role Bearer isn't accepted there. Doing it inline with the service client also needs no per-ticket ownership check (this is a trusted backfill)

edgeFunctions.name: enrich-lineup
edgeFunctions.purpose: The bill, from the people who were there. Venue first: "Seaside Park" on 2023-10-01 is the eleven acts of Sound on Sound, and a venue name plus an exact date is strong enough that it is NOT second-guessed by the ticket's coordinates - that ticket is pinned to the wrong Seaside Park, 150km away in New Jersey. City second, for festivals whose acts are filed under stage names rather than the site: Coachella's are "Sahara" and "Gobi", so the polo club never matches. A city name is much weaker evidence, so those results ARE held to the ticket's coordinates - "Manchester" on Bonnaroo's date otherwise returns the Etihad Stadium and a bar in New Hampshire. Best-effort throughout: a festival with no setlists is the normal case, not a failure.

edgeFunctions.name: enrich-pending-imports
edgeFunctions.purpose: Per run. The backlog is finite and shrinking, so a small batch drains it over a few hours while keeping any single run cheap and well inside the wall clock.

edgeFunctions.name: enrich-sweep
edgeFunctions.purpose: Scheduled enrichment sweep. Finds a small batch of PAST tickets still missing their admin-triggerable enrichment (sports results, theatre cast) and invokes the existing lookup functions for each — the same thing the app does lazily on view and the admin panel does on demand, but proactively on a cron so data stays fresh without anyone opening the ticket. Idempotent and capped, so it's safe to run often.

edgeFunctions.name: enrichment-worker
edgeFunctions.purpose: The single enrichment worker — drains the enrichment_jobs queue for every kind. See 20260813230000_enrichment_pipeline.sql for the why. Each tick: discover work (enqueue_enrichment_jobs), then per kind claim a small PACED batch and run its handler, marking each job done (attempted — data found or definitively none) or a transient retry. Because a 429 / 5xx becomes a backed-off retry rather than a "done", a burst can never silently mark a resolvable item unresolved, and the per-kind batch caps keep us under every provider's rate limit. Adding an enrichment kind = one handler here + one INSERT in enqueue_enrichment_jobs(). Phase 1 covers geocode (reuses geocode-venues/core.ts) and sports_result (drives sports-score-lookup). Auth: verify_jwt=false (config.toml) + shared x-cron-secret.

edgeFunctions.name: event-checkin
edgeFunctions.purpose: event-checkin — the morning-after "How was the show?" push. Runs daily via pg_cron at 15:00 UTC. For each user with an unrated event from the last couple of days it sends ONE push, named after the event and deep-linked to it. Fatigue-safe by three separate mechanisms, because this is the push that fires closest to a real moment and would be the most annoying to get wrong: 1. sent_event_checkins UNIQUE(user_id, ticket_id), written BEFORE the send. 2. One push per user per run, however many events they had. 3. capReengagement, so it counts against the daily re-engagement cap in send-notification. Auth: verify_jwt=false (config.toml) + shared x-cron-secret — mirrors on-this-day.

edgeFunctions.name: event-details

edgeFunctions.name: events-at
edgeFunctions.purpose: Given a photo cluster's DATE + TIME + GPS, ask Ticketmaster "what event happened here then?" and, if one lines up confidently, create the discovered-event card. This is the cross-verification finder for concert/show discovery (SAL2-390): photos are matched to a CONFIRMED real event by date/time/location, not to a name guessed off the image. When nothing matches (or there's no GPS) the caller falls back to visual identification.

edgeFunctions.purpose: Server-side geocoding sweep — the permanent fix for tickets that never got venue coordinates. ROOT CAUSE it fixes: geocode-venues was ONLY triggered opportunistically (a photo scan, or opening the map) and is RLS-scoped to one user. A ticket created through any of the six creation paths (gmail / forward / calendar / photo-import / manual / event-details) whose owner never hit one of those paths stayed at null coordinates forever — in prod, 81 well-named venues across every source had no coordinates. This sweep geocodes every active ticket with a venue and no coordinates, for ALL users, on a schedule, so it is self-healing for existing AND future tickets. pg_cron -> trigger_geocode_sweep() -> pg_net POST -> here -> tickets_needing_geocode() -> per-venue Nominatim lookup (reuses geocode-venues/core.ts verbatim) -> update coords. Auth: verify_jwt=false (pinned in config.toml); the only cred

edgeFunctions.name: notify-event-photos
edgeFunctions.purpose: Push + inbox when a friend adds photos to an event's shared album (retention Phase 3b). Called by the UPLOADER's client once per manual-upload batch (useEventDetails). Gated three ways so it can only reach the right people: (1) the uploader must be SHARING event photos — otherwise co-attendees literally can't see them, so a "come look" push would be a dead end; (2) friendship; (3) shared attendance (the recipient has their own ticket for the same canonical event). Deduped to one alert per (adder, recipient, event) via sent_event_photo_alerts, so re-uploading to the same album doesn't re-ping. verify_jwt stays TRUE (default): the caller's JWT is required for the gates. NOT in config.toml.

edgeFunctions.name: notify-message
edgeFunctions.purpose: Push + inbox notification for a new direct message. Called by the SENDER's client right after inserting a message. We authenticate the caller, confirm they and the recipient are accepted friends (mirroring the direct_messages insert RLS, so this can't be used to spam strangers), then hand off to send-notification which writes the inbox row, respects the user's notification_preferences, and sends the Expo push when a token exists.

edgeFunctions.name: notify-status
edgeFunctions.purpose: Push + inbox when a friend posts an event status (retention Phase 3, social loop). Statuses update live in-app via a realtime subscription (modules/status/hooks/useStatuses.ts), but a friend who isn't looking never learns a co-attendee posted a moment from a show they were both at. Called by the POSTER's client right after inserting the status. Gated on BOTH friendship AND shared attendance (the recipient must have their own ticket for the same canonical event) — so this can only reach people who were actually there, never broadcast a status to strangers. verify_jwt stays TRUE (default): the caller's JWT is required for the friendship check, exactly like notify-message. Do NOT add this function to config.toml's verify_jwt=false list.

edgeFunctions.name: notify-tag-prompt
edgeFunctions.purpose: Push a "tag your friend" nudge when a new ticket overlaps a friend's event. Client-invoked by the NEW ticket's owner right after creating it (mirrors notify-message). We authenticate the caller, confirm they own the (active, titled) ticket, and — only if the owner's OWN privacy allows being surfaced (mirroring suggest_event_attendees: allow_tagging + share_events + not only_me) — notify each accepted friend who already has the SAME event and isn't already linked to it. "Same event" is the canonical eventDedupeKey (shared catalog event_id, else title + DAY), NOT a raw lowercased title — the exact match public.suggest_event_attendees uses. A raw title match both over-fired (a friend's SAME show on a DIFFERENT date got a bogus "you're both going" push — the "Dave went to Hamilton on a different date" report) and under-fired (a "TICKET:"-prefixed or reformatted title missed a real overlap).

edgeFunctions.name: on-this-day
edgeFunctions.purpose: .then(noop, noop), NOT .catch() — a PostgREST builder is a lazy PromiseLike with no `catch`, so `.catch?.()` short-circuits and the insert is NEVER SENT. This function had zero api_usage_log rows for exactly that reason.

edgeFunctions.name: receive-forwarded-email

We verify the Svix signature, map the token to a user, fetch the full body from Resend (the webhook only carries metadata), and run it through the same parse/insert pipeline as a Gmail scan. Deploy with --no-verify-jwt: the caller is Resend, not a user — auth IS the signature. Required secrets: RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET, RESEND_API_KEY, INBOUND_EMAIL_DOMAIN (e.g. "abc123.resend.app"), plus the standard SUPABASE_URL / SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY.

Looks up what happened at the ticket's venue on its date via Ticketmaster (geo + date), and if the real event's name meaningfully differs from what the user saved, renames the ticket — preserving the original title. Fire-and-forget from enrichTicketImage; idempotent (skips once original_title is set).

edgeFunctions.name: venue-gazetteer-cron
edgeFunctions.purpose: Builds the coords → venue gazetteer from the ticket corpus we already collect. Every user's geocoded tickets — past events included — are thousands of real (venue name, coordinates) pairs. Rolled up they become public.venues, which the photo scan then uses to tell the night-event classifier "these photos were taken at Madison Square Garden" instead of asking a vision model to guess a venue off dark concert pixels. pg_cron -> trigger_venue_gazetteer() -> pg_net POST -> here -> venue_rollup_aggregate() (count-only, cross-user) -> rollupVenues() -> upsert venues. The rollup re-derives the WHOLE gazetteer from the WHOLE corpus every tick, so it is idempotent and self-correcting: a venue whose supporting tickets are deleted decays, and a bad row cannot persist once the data behind it changes. sharedModules.name: apiUsage.ts
sharedModules.purpose: How a provider call ended. 'ok' worked and returned data 'not_found' worked; the provider has nothing for this query. NOT a fault. 'error' something actually went wrong `success` answers the narrower question "did the call work", so a not_found row is success = true. Read outcome === 'ok' for "did we get data" — conflating the two is what made setlist-lookup read as a 100% failure when six of its seven failures were setlist.fm saying 404, i.e. "no setlist for this show".

sharedModules.name: artistName.ts
sharedModules.purpose: Words people append to an artist when typing a ticket by hand - "Black Keys Concert", "Justin Timberlake concert", "Ben Howard Concert ". Splitting on a separator only helps when there IS one, so these reached setlist.fm as an artist literally named "Black Keys Concert" and found nothing. Four real, heavily-documented artists sat in "concerts with no setlist" for exactly this reason. "tour" is deliberately absent. With no separator it would turn "Taylor Swift Eras Tour" into "Taylor Swift Eras", which is worse than leaving it alone.

sharedModules.name: autoAccept.ts
sharedModules.purpose: Minimum confidence for a source to bypass review WHEN NO SENDER SIGNAL IS AVAILABLE.

sharedModules.name: confidence.ts
sharedModules.purpose: Multi-signal confidence (beta #6). A single event can be evidenced by several INDEPENDENT sources — a Gmail/IMAP receipt, a device-calendar entry, a matched photo, an existing setlist. When more than one corroborates the SAME event, our confidence that it's real should climb toward certainty. We treat each source as independent evidence and combine with noisy-OR: combined = 1 - Π(1 - confidence_i) Two independent 0.7 signals → 0.91; three mid signals → ~0.94; a lone 0.55 stays 0.55. This is what pushes corroborated events toward the 90-100% the beta wants, while a single weak signal stays low. Repeated hits from the SAME source collapse to their strongest single confidence first (two Gmail emails for one show are one piece of evidence, not two).

sharedModules.name: contentAlert.ts
sharedModules.purpose: Build the push/inbox copy for a post-event content alert. Pure — no side effects, no I/O — so the exact wording is unit-tested. `eventTitle` is the ticket title (e.g. "Phish at MSG"); a blank/unknown title falls back to a neutral phrase rather than an empty string.

sharedModules.name: crypto.ts
sharedModules.purpose: AES-256-GCM application-layer encryption for credentials stored at rest (Gmail OAuth tokens, IMAP passwords). The key lives only in the edge-function runtime (TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY secret), never in the database — so a DB dump or a leaked row reveals only ciphertext. Satisfies CASA Tier 2 / OWASP ASVS V6 (cryptographic storage of sensitive data). ── Key rotation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Rotating the key used to be silently destructive. Every stored value was "enc:v1:<data>" with no record of WHICH key produced it, and only one key was ever loaded — so the moment TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY changed, every existing credential became permanently undecryptable, and the only symptom was `OperationError: Decryption failed` deep in a scan function. That is exactly what happened on 2026-08-08: six mailbox credentials died at once and it took reading edge-function lo

It was previously unreachable from Deno, and the cover-art module said so in its own comment - which is why that module answered a deliberately narrower question and a cricket ticket kept a photograph of a baseball stadium. This is the ONE copy. lib/ticketGrouping.ts re-exports it, so the chip row and the cover art can never disagree about what sport a ticket is.

sharedModules.name: eventShape.ts
sharedModules.purpose: Events with a field and a winner rather than two sides - golf, tennis, a fight card.

sharedModules.name: imapAllowlist.ts
sharedModules.purpose: Throws if the host/port is not an approved IMAP endpoint. Call before persisting or connecting to a user-supplied IMAP host.

sharedModules.name: imapError.ts
sharedModules.purpose: A rich, credential-safe one-line diagnostic for an IMAP / ImapFlow error. scan-imap used to record only `err.message`, which for ImapFlow is the generic "Command failed" on almost every failure. That cannot tell a REVOKED / wrong app password (`authenticationFailed`, code AUTHENTICATIONFAILED) from a TLS / network fault (ETIMEDOUT, ECONNREFUSED, …) — so a Yahoo connection that failed every scheduled scan for two weeks left `scan_runs.error_message = "IMAP connection failed: Command failed"` and nobody could see why. ImapFlow carries the real cause in PROPERTIES, and its error `response`/`responseText` are the SERVER's reply lines (e.g. "NO [AUTHENTICATIONFAILED]"), never the password the client sent — so they are safe to persist. Same lesson as store-email-connection/core.ts's errorText(): read the properties, not just `.message`.

sharedModules.name: notify.ts
sharedModules.purpose: Server-side push + in-app inbox notification. send-notification always writes the `notifications` inbox row first and only then consults notification_preferences, so a user who muted the push still finds it in the app. We keep that contract rather than pre-filtering here. The gateway runs send-notification with verify_jwt=true, so we authenticate with the service-role key. Its auth.getUser() resolves to no user for a service-role caller, which the send path explicitly allows (only the delete path needs a real user). `screen` follows the app's routing convention (see app/_layout.tsx and NotificationsScreen): a bare name resolves under the tab group ("tickets" -> /(tabs)/tickets), a leading slash routes as-is ("/review-imports").

sharedModules.name: notifyContent.ts
sharedModules.purpose: Re-engagement window. Only push "your setlist / score / cast is ready" for an event the user actually just attended. This is what keeps a back-catalogue import — which enqueues years of incomplete tickets at once — from blasting alerts about shows from 2016. The content is still saved either way; only the push is gated.

sharedModules.name: photoPrivacyScreen.ts
sharedModules.purpose: The privacy screen that decides whether a photo may be surfaced as event evidence. This lived in TWO verbatim copies — `screen-photos/core.ts` and an inline `privacyNote` + tool schema in `verify-photos/index.ts` — which is the same drift trap as the category classifier's four copies. Both call sites now import from here, so the wording can only be changed in one place. ── Why the "not about who is in the photo" clause exists ────────────────────── An audit on 2026-08-21 re-ran this screen over 96 already-approved photos that had never been verified. adminLibs.name: alerts.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Incident lifecycle and cascading notification for the health checks. The rule that makes this usable rather than noisy: **alerts fire on state transitions, not on state.** A check that has been down for six hours produced one tier-1 email when it broke, one tier-2 email when it stayed broken past the escalation window, and one "recovered" email at the end — not one per cron tick. Tier 1 is the first responder (Rahul). Tier 2 is pulled in only when tier 1 hasn't cleared the incident within `escalate_after_minutes` — the "what if he's travelling" case from the 8/15 review.

adminLibs.name: analytics.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Behavioural analytics — activation, capture effectiveness, enrichment coverage, engagement. Complements the existing count-based panels. Counts tell you how big the system is; these tell you whether it is WORKING: are users activating, which capture path produces tickets, is the enrichment queue keeping up, and are people coming back. Every database figure is aggregated in Postgres (migration 020). Reducing rows in JS would be silently wrong past 1000 rows — the PostgREST cap this project keeps running into.

The provider's own dashboard can tell you a quota is nearly spent; only this can tell you which edge function spent it. Every figure is aggregated in Postgres (016_api_usage_summary.sql). Reducing rows in JS would be silently wrong: PostgREST caps responses at 1000 rows on this project regardless of .limit(), and this table is already past 12k. adminLibs.purpose: Mobile crash / unhandled-exception feed, from PostHog's `$exception` events. PostHog is already collecting these (44 in the 30 days before this shipped), so this needs no new integration or credential, just a read. adminLibs.name: events.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Helpers for the canonical-event surface (the `public.events` table the app resolves every ticket to). adminLibs.name: invite.ts
adminLibs.purpose: One-time invite / password-set token for the admin panel. Only the SHA-256 hash is persisted (admin_users.invite_token_hash). The raw token is embedded in the invite URL emailed to the invitee, so a DB leak never yields a valid, usable token — a matching URL is still required. 32 random bytes → 43-char base64url string; brute-forcing the hash space is not feasible.

adminLibs.name: message-templates.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Pre-written email + push-notification templates for the admin Email and Notifications pages. Picking one pre-fills the composer so common messages don't have to be typed from scratch — edit the fields before sending. Text in [square brackets] is a placeholder: swap it for the real detail before you send. Nothing here is substituted automatically. To add a template, append to the relevant array — the pickers pick it up automatically. Email bodies use blank lines to separate paragraphs (the branded renderer turns each blank-line-delimited block into a paragraph).

adminLibs.name: ops-cycle.ts
adminLibs.purpose: One full monitoring cycle: check → reconcile → remediate → verify → notify. Shared by the cron route and the "Run now" button on /health so both do exactly the same thing. The ordering matters: remediation runs *before* notification, and a verification pass re-reconciles afterwards. A transient blip that auto-heals within the cycle therefore resolves silently — nobody is emailed about a problem that no longer exists by the time the email would have been sent.

adminLibs.name: pages.ts
adminLibs.purpose: The canonical list of admin pages. Extracted out of components/sidebar.tsx so ONE table drives three things that must never disagree: what the sidebar renders, what the per-admin page allowlist offers, and what the proxy enforces. When they were separate, a page could be hidden from the nav while still being reachable by typing the URL. `maxLevel` is the CAPABILITY bar (1 = Super Admin … 4 = Support) and is unchanged. The allowlist layers ON TOP of it — it can only ever narrow access, never widen it. See canAccessPage().

adminLibs.name: pending-imports.ts
adminLibs.purpose: How many distinct users are behind the unreviewed-import backlog. `pending_imports` counts EVENTS, not people: one user with a linked inbox routinely contributes dozens, so the raw total reads as a user count and badly overstates reach. Every surface that shows the total shows this next to it. Counted in Postgres, not JS. PostgREST caps a response at `db-max-rows` (1000 on this project), so `select user_id` + a Set silently undercounts the moment the backlog passes that — and the backlog is already four figures.

adminLibs.name: posthog.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Read-only PostHog query client for admin analytics (build adoption, etc.). PostHog's ingestion ("project") API keys are write-only, so querying needs a **Personal API key** scoped to `query:read` (+ `project:read`): POSTHOG_API_KEY — personal API key (starts with `phx_`) POSTHOG_PROJECT_ID — numeric project id (defaults to 489677, the Salty project) POSTHOG_HOST — API host (defaults to https://us.posthog.com) The panel only ever runs read-only HogQL SELECTs against this connection. Leave POSTHOG_API_KEY unset to disable the feature — pages show a "not connected" notice (same pattern as the v2 database / Beta Signups page) instead of erroring.

adminLibs.name: remediation.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Auto-remediation for health incidents. The safety property that makes this acceptable against production: **the model never writes an action, it only chooses one from the allow-list below.** Every entry is a bounded, reversible operation that a human would run from the admin panel anyway. An LLM that returns anything not in this list is ignored and the incident escalates to a person instead. Deterministic rules run first and cover the cases we already understand. The model tier (lib/llm/ladder.ts) is only consulted for incidents with no matching rule, and only when `ai_triage_enabled` is on — so the common path costs nothing and behaves identically every time.

adminLibs.name: sort.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Server-side, in-memory row sorting for fully-loaded (non-paginated) tables that pair with the URL-driven <SortLink> header. Reads `sort`/`dir` from the page's searchParams; when no known sort key is set, falls back to `fallback` (typically newest-first). Nulls always sort last; strings compare numerically-aware.
